content.title: RULES EVERY NEW PARENT NEEDS BEFORE THE BABY {{SLEEPS}}
facts: **Room temp first** – keep the nursery between 68-72°F; overheating is a bigger risk to safe sleep than most parents realize.
**Feet-to-foot** – place baby with feet at the bottom of the crib so they can't scoot under a blanket.
**Skip the crib bumpers** – they look cozy but add suffocation risk with zero proven safety benefit.
**1 safe sleep space** – crib or bassinet only, nothing soft underneath, nothing extra inside.
**Burp for 2 minutes** – after every feed, to cut down on painful gas and late-night waking.
**Batch your meals on Sunday** – 30 minutes of prep now saves you from surviving on crackers during week one.
**Nap when they nap** – just once a day for the first month; sleep debt hits harder than people warn you.
**Write down feed times** – a simple notes app log saves you from guessing at 3am whether they're actually hungry.
**Ask for help early** – before you're desperate, not after; recovery and bonding both go smoother with support.
**Follow along** – for more daily health tips like this.
content.caption:
A few things from the list are worth sitting with longer. Room temperature matters more than most new parents expect — an overheated nursery has been linked to higher sleep risk than almost any other factor, so a simple thermometer on the wall does more than another baby monitor gadget ever will. The burp habit isn't just about comfort either: trapped air presses on a baby's still-developing digestive system, and even one skipped burp can mean an extra hour of fussing that looks like 'just colic' but isn't. And napping when they nap isn't a cute suggestion — sleep debt in the first weeks compounds fast and is one of the biggest predictors of postpartum exhaustion spiraling into something harder to bounce back from. Every baby and every parent is different, so take what fits your household and leave the rest.
